title: The Purple Jacket
paragraphs: In olden times among the Turkic encampments there was a custom: into the trousseau of a girl who was to marry they would place, among other things, a purple jacket. The jacket was laid at the very bottom of the dowry chest, and it was hoped that the woman would never put it on.

The purple jacket was a garment that could bring ruin upon a man. For if a woman put it on and went up onto the roof of the house, to the chimney, or into the village square — anywhere that all might see her — it meant: «I do not love my husband, my husband torments me, I married against my heart, I wish to divorce, I am in a hard plight — help me.» Then the village folk would come to that woman's aid and would censure her husband. For a man this was reckoned a great shame.

For that reason men would try to settle their troubles with their wives without resort to violence, with love and respect, and moreover by making important concessions to the lady. Otherwise they knew that the woman would put on the purple jacket.

A man whose wife had donned the purple jacket would not only be forced into divorce, but could scarcely marry again with ease. For everyone knew that a man who drove his wife to wear the purple jacket was no husband at all. No one would give a daughter again to a man who showed a woman no respect and used violence against her; for him to marry a second time was very hard. It is said that for this very reason the number of women who suffered violence was almost nil.

If a woman put on her purple jacket, then flowing waters would halt, the hands that milked cows, spun wool, and wove kilims would stop; elderly mothers and grandmothers would leave their work and rise in defence of the woman who had been driven to wear the purple jacket.

At that hour, if there were wedding feast or zurna and drum or any other merriment about, all of it would fall silent. For a married woman's putting on the purple jacket, her falling into a hard plight, was taken as something like death.
The husband of a woman who had donned the purple jacket could not step outside his house, could not go to the teahouse, and no one would look him in the face.
Violence against a woman is unacceptable. When society holds the protection of women to be a duty of conscience, oppression finds no place.

title: Friendship and Love
paragraphs: — Write quarrel and strife upon a leaf of the tree, so that when autumn comes the leaves dry and fall, and quarrel and strife vanish.
— Write anger upon a cloud, so that the rain may fall, the clouds disperse, and anger vanish.
— Write hatred upon the snow, so that the sun may rise, the snows melt, and hatred vanish.
— Write friendship and love upon the hearts of newborn babes, so that they may grow, and friendship and love may spread throughout the world.
Write strife, anger, and hatred upon things that pass, that they may be lost; but write friendship and love upon hearts, that they may endure forever and go out into the world.

title: Early Marriage
paragraphs: I had just finished university and begun work as a teacher at a school. One day I was sitting in the teachers' room looking over the pupils' examination papers. I was rubbing out the wrong answers of the girl pupils and correcting them so that they might get good marks and pass into the higher form.

At that moment someone came into the teachers' room and asked with curiosity why I was altering the girls' examination papers. I said: «If these girls fail the examination, their fathers will take them out of school and give them in marriage at twelve or thirteen. But if they pass into the higher form, their age of marriage will be at least fifteen or sixteen. And in that time even the laziest pupil is bound to learn something in class.»
About half an hour later our headmaster called me and asked what I had been doing in the teachers' room. I said I had been looking over the examination papers.
— You met someone in the teachers' room. What did you say to him? — he asked.
— Did that man complain of me to you? — I asked.
— Not at all! The man came to me and said he had come to inspect the school, but that there was no need of it whatever.
— Why? — I wondered.
— Because you have a wise young teacher. Please convey my thanks to him, — he said.
A teacher's small care can change a girl's fate. Early marriage robs children of learning; let us not turn a blind eye to it.

title: What Breaks a Marriage
paragraphs: Between a father and his newly married young son such a story takes place.
The father asks his son to bring a sheet of white paper, a pen, and an eraser.
— Why? — asks the son.
— Just bring them, — says the father.
The son brings the pen and paper, but cannot find an eraser.
— Go and buy an eraser too and bring it, — says the father.
The son is much surprised, yet he goes and buys an eraser, brings it, and sits down beside his father.
— Write, — says the father.
— What shall I write?
— Write whatever you like.
The son writes a sentence.
— Now erase it, — says the father.
The son erases it.
— Write another sentence.
— For heaven's sake, Father, what do you want?
— Write something again.
The son writes. His father makes him erase what he has written once more.
After this writing and erasing has been repeated several times, the father asks:
— Is the paper still white?
— Yes, it is white, Father. But what does all this mean?
The father lays his hand on his son's shoulder and says:

— Yes, my son, marriage is a thing that cannot do without an eraser... To erase some of the things you will see in your wife and not approve of, you must carry an eraser with you. And your wife must have such an eraser too, to erase the unpleasant things you will do. For if you do not, in a few days your page of marriage will be black as night...
If in your life you expect mutual love and respect, both of you will show this to each other. And the eraser — never forget it!
Marriage is the art of being able to forgive. For love and respect to endure, both sides must know how to «erase» each other's faults.

title: Advice for Those Who Marry
paragraphs: From the counsel of worldly-wise elders to a young couple who are marrying:
«...Do not compare your marriage with the marriages of others; do not say, look how so-and-so's husband or wife is this way or that... Never!
Do not seek perfection. None of us is perfect. Do not dig into each other's past; it is called «the past» for a reason.
Do not expect your partner to read your mind. Alas, no one can. Say openly everything you want or do not want; believe that by talking you can settle everything.

Along with living together, accept that each of you has a private world of your own. It is well known that hedgehogs draw near their mates only as far as the length of their quills; they know that if they come too close, the quills will pierce and their mate will be hurt. You too, so as not to hurt each other, refrain from meddling in one another's private world.
In your marriage strive to be not each other's master or slave, but companions.
Do not promise that «everything will be fine» — alas, it is not. Instead say, «if you fall into trouble, I am always beside you.»
Even if you have been at odds all day, before you sleep say to each other «Good night!» — however hard it may be. Be sure to say it, so that your tomorrow may dawn in peace...»
A happy marriage lies not in comparison and the search for perfection, but in open speech, in respect, and in reverence for each other's private world.

title: I Kiss Your Eyes
paragraphs: Do you know why people say «I kiss your eyes»?
It is the eyes that feel most keenly the ache of longing; and for that reason it is they who most deserve the meeting.
Those who long the most are the most worthy of reunion. Love gives back their due to those who have borne its labour.

title: The Rose
paragraphs: Water a rose too much and it rots; water it too little and it withers; water it rightly and it lives.
In love as in upbringing, measure is the essence. Neither excessive pressure nor indifference — measured care keeps a thing alive.

title: True Love
paragraphs: There was once an island where all the feelings lived.
One day word spread that this island was sinking. The feelings began in haste to prepare to leave the island.

Love was in no hurry to leave the island. For she waited until the very last moment, as if sure that a miracle would save her. When the island was all but submerged, Love at last decided to ask for help.
At that moment Wealth was drawing away from the island in a very great boat.
Love asks: «Wealth, can you take me with you?» Wealth says: «No, I cannot. In my boat I have gold and silver in abundance; there is no room for you.»
Love then turns to Pride, who is sailing past in a very fine sailing boat, and asks for help: «Pride, please help me.»
Pride answers: «I cannot help you, Love. You are very wet; you would ruin my sail.»
Sadness was nearby. Love asks her for help as well: «Sadness, may I come with you?»
Sadness says: «Alas, Love, I am so sad that I need to be alone.»
Happiness was not far from Love, yet she was so excited that she did not hear Love's call.

Suddenly a voice comes: «Love, come, let us go with me.» Love feels so lucky and happy that it does not even occur to her to ask who it is that has held out a hand. When they reach the shore, the one who helped Love leaves her there and goes on his way.
Once on shore, realizing how much she owes, Love tells a wise man she meets what has befallen her and asks: «I wonder — who was it that helped me?»
The wise man answers: «It was Time.»
«Time? But why did he help me?» Love asks.
The wise man smiles: «Because only Time knows how important and precious Love is.»
Only time knows the worth of true love. Sincere love time keeps alive; the false it extinguishes and makes forgotten.

title: What Women Have Endured in This World...
paragraphs: What women have endured in this world...
Even in fairy tales they fitted her only to be either a witch or a stepmother...
In stories what was not said of woman.
She could never simply be herself; yet in this world her name ought to have been one who gives life, who raises, who loves without asking return.
Woman...
They said to her: long of hair, short of wit.
They said to her: your hands are floury — sit in your place, meddle with no one.
Ah, woman, what you have endured in this world.
Few knew her worth.
Few could see her love, her heart, her goodness.
When you asked for your right you were bad; when you were silent, pure.
When you showed your love, some took you for their master.
Sometimes those whom you raised to the heavens with your affection preferred to remain there and forgot you.
They did not ask what was the matter, how you were.
They did not say whether you were there or not.
They forgot that you had a soul.
They forgot that you were human.
They made you ill, crushed you, looked past you...
And you had no intent but to beautify, to help, to make better.
Your soul wandered this world in need of love.
They spoke of paradise and made you live through hell.
Looking into your eyes they denied even what they saw there. They did not hear the cry that rose from within you.
She loved most of all to be a mother, loved to look with love into her child's eyes. In this world only her child's embrace felt sincere to her.
Where woman is not valued there is neither peace nor love. To see her labour and her heart is society's duty.

title: The Woman and the Mirror
paragraphs: A woman wakes early in the morning and looks in the mirror. She sees that three hairs remain on her head.
«Hmm... — she says. — Today I shall braid my hair...» She braids it, and the day goes splendidly...
The next day she wakes and looks in the mirror again... She sees that two hairs remain on her head.
«Hmm... — she says. — Today I shall part my hair in two...» She does as she says and again spends a lovely day...
The day after that, when she wakes, she sees in the mirror that a single hair remains on her head.
«Never mind, so be it... — she says. — Today I shall make a ponytail...» And so she does, and spends a most magnificent day...
One more day she looks in the mirror and sees that no hair remains on her head at all.
«Oh my!.. — she cries out with joy. — How wonderful — today I have no hair trouble at all!»
Everything depends on the angle of view. One who cannot create happiness within cannot take it from another either — learn to walk even in the rain.

title: The Red Dress
paragraphs: The red dress hung forgotten in my mother's wardrobe. Beside the worn, faded clothes she had worn all her life, this red dress seemed almost to give off light.
I came to visit my mother and the moment I saw her I understood that she was living the last moments of her life.
Seeing the red dress I said to her:
— Mother, what a beautiful dress! I have never seen it on you, — I said.
— I never wore it, — she said softly. — Sit beside me, my lovely girl; before I leave this world I want to give you a lesson.
I sat on the edge of the bed. My mother drew a deep breath. «I have little time left,» she said, and went on:
— Though I always thought I had taught you good things, I have now understood that I taught you many wrong ones.
— What kind of talk is that, Mother?

— Listen to me. I always believed that a good woman must not think of herself first. I was always to think of others before myself. I had to fulfil the wishes of this one and that — always of everyone. And my own wishes were crushed beneath the wishes of others. Who knows — perhaps one day my wishes too would have come true. But that day never came. My whole life passed in self-sacrifice — the sacrifices I made for your father, for your brothers and sisters, for you.
— That is so, Mother; you did everything a mother could do.

— Ah, my girl, neither what I did for you nor what I did for them brought me any good. Do you understand? I never asked anything for myself! Your father is in the next room now, looking nervously at the walls. When the doctor told him I was living my last days he came to me and said:
— You must not die, do you hear me? What am I to do after you? — he said.

— My girl, I always threw myself into fire and ember for you. All seven days of the week... The first to wake in the house and the last to sleep was always I. The burnt loaves, the smallest scraps — I always ate them. Every kopeck I saved I spent on your clothes, your books — often needlessly. Never once in my life did I go shopping and buy something lovely for myself. Only that red dress you saw last year. I had a little money put by for the repair of the washing machine. When I bought the dress and came home your father distressed me greatly:
— Where will you wear this dress? Are you going to the opera? — he said.
In truth he was right. Apart from trying it on in the shop, I never wore that dress.

— Ah, my girl, I used to think that if a person does not think of herself in this world, she will be happy in the next. But I no longer believe that. I think God wants us to fulfil our wishes in this very world and now. If a miracle happened now and I could rise from this bed, I would be a very different person.
These were my mother's last words to me:
— My girl, — she said, — do not go my way. Promise me.
I promised my mother, and she drew her last breath.
One who always forgets herself will one day see that she has lived none of her own life. Love others, but give yourself the right to live as well.

title: Do Not Let Your Hearts Part
paragraphs: Why do people shout when they argue? If a person is beside you, what need is there to shout? Can one not speak with him calmly? When you grow angry, why do you shout?
When people are displeased with each other and argue, their hearts draw apart. To cross that distance and hear one another they must shout. The angrier they are, the louder they shout.
And what happens when people fall in love?
They do not shout; on the contrary, they speak softly. For their hearts are very near, and the distance between them is very small.
And what happens when their love grows still stronger?

They fall silent; they only whisper, and this love draws them still closer. In the end even a whisper becomes needless for them — they simply look at each other and understand everything without words. This happens only between two people who love each other.
Therefore when you argue, do not let your hearts part; do not speak words that could widen the distance between you. For one day that distance may grow so great that you cannot turn back.
A shout is the sound of the distance between hearts. In a quarrel do not speak words that will widen that distance, or return will grow hard.

title: Yellow and Red Flowers
paragraphs: Yellow flowers set in a house window meant «there is a sick person in this house; do not make a noise as you pass,» and red flowers meant «there is a girl of marriageable age in this house; mind your speech as you pass.»
A culture of sensitive communication built on fine signs teaches people wordless respect. A warning is sometimes given without a shout.

title: Beware of Those You Love
paragraphs: It was a sunny day. A woman said to the man sitting beside her in the park:
— Look, that child in the red shirt swinging on the swing is my son, — she said.
The man smiled:
— Mashallah, you have a fine son, — he said.
— And the child in the blue shirt on the other swing is my son too.
Then he glanced at his watch and called to his son:
— Jamil, it is time to go home now; come, let us go.
The child, still swinging, begged:
— Five more minutes, Father, please — only five minutes, — he pleaded.
When the man nodded in the sense of «all right,» the child went on swinging with joy.
After a while the man rose and called to his son again:
— Jamil, my son, let us go now; it has grown late.
Again the child did not want to go:
— Please, Father, five more minutes — just five minutes, — he turned to his father.
When the man said «very well,» the child began to swing again with a happy smile on his face.
At last the woman could not contain herself and said, with a hidden admiration in her voice:
— What a patient father you are, — she said.
The man smiled:

— This is not patience, madam, — he said. — Last year I lost my elder son Kamal here, on the nearby road, when a drunken driver struck him while he was riding his bicycle. I had never been able to give Kamal enough of my time. Now I would do anything to be with him five minutes longer. I promised myself I would not make the same mistake with Jamil.

— Each time he says «five more minutes, Father,» he thinks he has gained five extra minutes for play. But the true gainer is I, for I can watch him at play five minutes longer and take a great joy from it.
Every extra moment you spend with those you love is a blessing. Before it is too late, give them five minutes more today.

title: The Beloved Is One Who Gives Love to People
paragraphs: Many years ago in China a girl named Li-Li married and began to live in the same house with her husband and her mother-in-law. But before long she understood that getting on with her mother-in-law was very hard. Their characters were utterly different, and this led them to quarrel often. By Chinese tradition this was not a pleasing state of affairs and gave rise to the discontent of those around them.

After a few months the endless daughter-in-law and mother-in-law struggles became a torment of hell both for the young woman and for her husband, caught in the middle. Believing that something must be done, the young woman ran to an old friend of her father's, a spice merchant, and poured out her grief. The old man prepared her a medicine from plants and charged her to add a little of it every day for three months to the meals she cooked for her mother-in-law. The poison was to be given little by little, so that it would not be known that the daughter-in-law had killed the mother-in-law.

The old man charged the young woman to treat her mother-in-law very kindly and cook her the tastiest dishes, so that no one — especially her husband — should grow suspicious. Returning home with joy, Li-Li did exactly as the old man had said.

Every day she cooked the finest meals and dripped «poison» drop by drop into her mother-in-law's plate. So that no one should suspect, she treated her very well. After a while her mother-in-law had changed greatly and looked on her as her own daughter. Feeling herself under a heavy burden, the young woman went in remorse to the spice merchant's shop and begged the old man for a medicine that would cleanse from her mother-in-law's blood the poison she had given her until then. She no longer wished the old woman to die.

The old man looked at Li-Li standing before him, burst into laughter, and said: «Dear Li-Li, what I gave you was only vitamins. The real poison was in your own mind. As you treated her well, that poison melted away and gave place to love; and so you became true mother and child.»
The real poison is often in our own minds. As you treat the one before you with love, hatred melts, and an enemy turns into a friend.

title: Can a Broken Heart Love Again?
paragraphs: Someone asked a dervish:
— Can a broken heart love again?
— Yes, it can, — said the dervish.
The man said to the dervish: — Have you ever drunk water from a broken vessel?
The dervish: — You tell me — have you ever given up drinking water because a vessel was broken?
Though the heart breaks, it does not give up loving. Just as one does not give up water because a vessel is broken, so a person goes on loving.

title: The Mother-of-Pearl Flower
paragraphs: In the courtroom the plight of an eighty-year-old couple whose divorce suit was being heard brought bitter tears to everyone... The judge, glancing at the eyes of the stubborn-gazed, silent grandmother, hollowed by weeping, addressed the elderly woman in a stern voice:
— Tell us, auntie, why do you wish to divorce? — he asked.
After drawing a deep breath the elderly woman began in a constricted voice:
— This man has worn me out; for a full fifty years he has made me sick of life..., — she said and fell silent.

A long silence settled over the hall. The silence was broken by a journalist's photo-flash. Who knows under what headline this event would appear in the papers after a fifty-year life. Many journalists were following the hearing. What would the woman say? Everyone was listening to her. The elderly woman's eyes filled and she went on: — I had a mother-of-pearl flower, one I loved very much... He does not know... It was fifty years ago. From among the roses he gave me I plucked a leaf, sprouted it, and planted it. We had no child; I took this flower for my child. After a while I saw that the flower had begun to fade.

Then I vowed that every night I would wake before the sun rose and water this rose. Fifty years have passed, and this man never once rose in the night and said «let me water this flower.» Until last night... That night my strength failed and I had fallen asleep; I could not wake... I have spent fifty years with such a man. I gave him my life, my hope, everything. From him I saw nothing. I assure you I can live my life better without him.
The judge addressed the greybeard:
— Have you anything to say, grandfather? — he asked.
Leaning on his stick, with a guilty look on his face, the elderly man turned toward the judge and began:

— I did my military service as a gardener. I laboured so that that garden might grow fair and strong. I met Fatima there too. I gave her bouquets of the loveliest flowers. When we were newly married she complained of a pain in her neck, so I took her to the doctor. The doctor said: «If she sleeps a very long time without waking, the muscles in her neck will stiffen and her condition will worsen. Every night let her break her sleep and wake, and walk about a little.» My wife did not heed the doctor's word... And my word carried no weight either... In those days, by chance, our flower began to fade. I said to her: «If you rise at night and water the flower, it will come to life.» I asked her to promise, and she promised...
Every night I woke her and watched. I watched that woman I loved as she watered the flower she took for her child. Every night it was as if I myself became that flower...
Grandfather fell silent a little and then went on again:

— Every night after she slept I would wake — to empty the water from the pot. The mother-of-pearl flower does not like to be watered at night, Your Honour... But last night... what can I say, this old age... I too could not wake... The flower might have gone without water, but my wife would have faced complications in her health... Because I did not wake her she held me guilty... I did not raise my voice; I kept silent...
At that moment everyone in the hall, journalists included, was in tears...
Love is sometimes hidden not in words but in care borne in silence through the years. Let us protect those we love; let us stay far from breaking hearts.

title: I Love You
paragraphs: They say that a nightingale fell in love with a white rose... Every night he would go and settle beside her and declare his love. But the white rose showed indifference to the nightingale's feelings and paid no heed to his love.

One day the nightingale once more gathered all his courage, settled beside the white rose, and told her that he loved her madly. But the rose snapped at the nightingale: «Leave me alone; I do not love you!» Though the nightingale insisted, the rose rejected him.

This love grew so strong that the nightingale was shaken with despair; begging the rose's pardon he plucked a thorn from her, drove it with all his strength into his heart, and dyed the snow-white rose red with his blood!

The rose, late though it was, understood that the nightingale had truly loved her very much. But what use! It was already far too late. Beneath the branches of the rose dyed red the nightingale closed his eyes forever.
From that day forth red roses have carried the meaning «I LOVE YOU.»
True love is sometimes understood very late. Value the one who loves you in the moment you love — fear having to say «too late.»

title: Loving from Afar
paragraphs: Two friends meet. Between them such a talk takes place:
— It seems I have fallen for a girl.
— How fine! Does she know?
— She does not.
— Then why do you not draw near and confess?

— I would, but I fear the upset of my order. All of a sudden, standing where I am, I shall open trouble on my head and fall into love and suchlike. We shall start going to the cinema, to the theatre, walking hand in hand. This business has its sulks, its makings-up, its putting on airs with «why did you look at her,» «why did you eye that one.» And if in the end there is to be a parting, what need of all this to-do?
Better that I love that girl just from afar.
Sometimes a person, from fear of losing, shrinks from putting love into words. But a love unlived is a loss as well.

title: What Is Loyalty?
paragraphs: It is not to forget,
not to turn your back in a hard day,
not to shut the doors...
Not to laugh while your friend weeps,
to sigh with him through every bitterness — that is loyalty...
It is not merely a word...
Loyalty means to be of one heart with your friend,
a balm to the wounded,
water to the thirsty,
and at last, loyalty is «to understand» — not to cast away a rose because of its thorn.
Loyalty is not to abandon in a hard day, not to cast away a rose because of its thorn. It is not a word but a deed.
